pretreatments.description: Biological pretreatment: A method based on the joint action of native microbiota of Agave bagasse composed mainly of Clostridium, Lactobacillus, and Enterobacter, described as a core microbiome of lignocellulosic biomasses. This core microbiota primarily hydrolyzes xylan, converting it into volatile fatty acids which were simulated solely as acetic acid to simplify the study. The enzymatic pretreatment unit was one of the scenarios that operated at a high-solid loading combined with a high percentage of solubilization. The biological pretreatment operated at the highest solids loading among scenarios but with a low solubilization percentage, resulting in 8 ton/d of bagasse solubilized. It is also a scenario that reached a high solubilization percentage. The biological pretreatment reached 100% solubilization of the xylan fraction. Therefore, a higher solubilization percentage requires the action of microorganisms that hydrolyze cellulose, which undoubtedly requires increasing the hydraulic retention time in the pretreatment section.

Enzymatic pretreatment: Based on the action of the commercial enzyme cocktail, Cellulase 50XL. This enzyme cocktail was simulated to a dose of 293 endoglucanase units (EGU)/g of bagasse working in a 50 mM citrate buffer pH 6. This enzyme preparation released mainly glucose along with galactose, arabinose, and other sugars. These sugars represented 69% of the total chemical oxygen demand (COD) simulated for this pretreatment. The enzymatic pretreatment is a scenario that reached the highest solubilization among scenarios, 12 ton/d (obtained by multiplying the total volatile solids conversion by the mass flow), of which 94% were converted into methane. The enzymatic pretreatment unit was one of the scenarios that operated at a high-solid loading combined with a high percentage of solubilization.

Dilute acid pretreatment: Solubilized all xylan and partially cellulose in 1.8% HCl under soft operating conditions, which recovered sugars and eliminated the generation of inhibitors. The dilute acid pretreatment had the highest percentage of solubilization but operated at a low-solid loading. The dilute acid pretreatment solubilized ca. 50% of cellulose – the majority fraction of feedstock – outperforming other pretreatments in efficiency. It is a scenario where the solid loadings were optimized to recover the maximum soluble matter.

Steam explosion pretreatment: Solubilized xylan producing a mixture of sugars and acetic acid. The pretreatment was performed in a plug flow reactor coupled to a flask tank where the instant depressurization takes place. The base scenario considered that the Agave bagasse was directly methanized after milling. The steam explosion pretreatment generated low concentrations of furfural (0.7 g/L) and hydroxymethylfurfural (0.12 g/L). It is a scenario that reached the highest solubilization among scenarios, 12 ton/d (obtained by multiplying the total volatile solids conversion by the mass flow), of which 94% were converted into methane. The steam explosion pretreatment operated at the lowest solids loading among scenarios with a low percentage of solubilization that resulted in just 2 ton/d of bagasse solubilized.

Bioprocess Conditioning: Biomass conditioning involved two rounds of shredding and grinding to reduce the size of particles. This was followed by screening to bring a final size of 3 ± 0.5 mm. The resulting ground biomass was then sent to a tank where it is hydrated and mechanically conveyed to the pretreatment section, as shown in Fig. 1.
